_meta.name: CrimeGPT section-mapping evaluation set
_meta.purpose: Measure the accuracy and stability of app.ai.legal.map_sections() on realistic plain-language complaints. This is a held-out yardstick, NOT training/tuning data. Do not tune prompts, retrieval, or thresholds against these cases — that would turn an honest baseline into an overfit number.
_meta.how_to_run: python scripts/section_eval.py   (writes section_eval_results.json + section_eval_report.md alongside this file)
_meta.expected_sections_are_provisional: Every `expected` list below is the author's reading of the BNS and MUST be verified against the bare acts in data/bns_bnss_bsa/ before the scores are trusted. `verified` starts false; flip it to true per case once a human has checked the section against BNS.txt. The runner reports how many cases are still unverified so a score built on unchecked ground truth cannot masquerade as final.
_meta.count_note: 21 cases. The build request enumerated theft(3)+hurt(2)+house-trespass(2)+CBT(2)+cheating(2)+intimidation(2)=13 in-scope multi, +6 single-offence types, +2 out-of-scope = 21 (the round '20' in the request is one short of its own breakdown; no requested crime type was dropped).

scoring.top1: primary expected section code appears in the model's selected sections
scoring.recall: expected sections found / expected sections total
scoring.precision: selected sections that are expected / selected sections total
scoring.stability: agreement of the selected-code set across the 3 runs

_meta.act_scope_note: map_sections() maps BNS offences only (retrieve_offences is act='BNS'). Expected sections are therefore BNS-only; BNSS/BSA are out of scope for this metric by design.

cases.complaint: I run a mobile phone shop. This afternoon while I was busy attending to a customer, an unknown man standing near the counter quietly picked up a new handset kept on display and walked out of the shop without paying for it. When I noticed, he had already left on a two-wheeler.
cases.notes: Plain dishonest taking of movable property without consent -> BNS 303 theft.

cases.complaint: In the afternoon our whole family had gone to a relative's wedding and the house was empty. A man entered our house through the open front door, went into the bedroom and took my wife's gold chain and about fifteen thousand rupees in cash kept in the almirah, and left. A neighbour saw an unknown man coming out of our house.

expected.title: Theft in a dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship, etc

cases.notes: Theft committed inside a dwelling house (no breaking) -> aggravated theft BNS 305; ordinary theft 303 also applies.

cases.complaint: I was walking home along the main road at about 8 in the evening. Two men came up fast behind me on a motorcycle, and the man riding pillion suddenly grabbed the gold chain from around my neck, pulled it off and they sped away before I could catch them.
cases.notes: Sudden forcible grabbing of a chain from the person -> BNS 304 snatching (a defined offence distinct from ordinary theft). Watch whether the model returns 303 instead.

cases.complaint: There was an argument with my neighbour over parking. In anger he punched me hard on the face two or three times. My nose started bleeding and my lip was cut. I was treated at the local clinic and given some medicine.
cases.notes: Simple bodily pain/bleeding caused intentionally, no weapon, not grievous -> BNS 115 voluntarily causing hurt.

cases.complaint: My neighbour came to my door holding an iron rod. Over an old dispute he swung it at me and hit my left forearm with full force. The bone was fractured and I had to have a plaster cast put on at the hospital. The doctor said the arm is broken in two places.

expected.title: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means

cases.notes: Fracture (grievous hurt) inflicted with a dangerous weapon (iron rod) -> BNS 118, and 117 voluntarily causing grievous hurt.

cases.complaint: Late at night I heard a noise in my courtyard. When I went out with a torch I found an unknown man had come inside the compound of my house over the gate, without any permission, and was standing near the veranda in the dark. When I shouted he jumped over the wall and ran off.
cases.notes: Unauthorised entry into a house/compound without breaking, at night -> BNS 329 house-trespass.

cases.complaint: At night while we were sleeping, someone broke open the latch of the back door of our house and got inside. We woke up when we heard the almirah being opened. He had pulled out clothes and papers looking for valuables. When my husband switched on the light the man ran out through the same door.
cases.notes: Breaking open a fastening (latch) to enter a dwelling at night -> house-breaking, BNS 330/331. Watch for 332/333 variants.

cases.complaint: Before going abroad for six months I gave two lakh rupees in cash to a close neighbour whom I trusted, and asked him to keep it safely and return it when I came back. Now that I have returned he is flatly denying that I ever gave him any money and refuses to return a single rupee.
cases.notes: Property entrusted, then dishonestly misappropriated/converted -> BNS 316 criminal breach of trust (not ordinary theft).

cases.complaint: I gave my gold ornaments weighing about sixty grams to a goldsmith to melt and make into new jewellery, and paid his making charges in advance. When I went to collect the new jewellery he kept postponing, and now I have found that he sold off my gold and has shut down his shop and is not answering calls.
cases.notes: Gold entrusted for a specific purpose, dishonestly disposed of -> BNS 316. May be confused with cheating (318).

cases.complaint: I saw an advertisement online for a used car at a good price. The seller convinced me it was genuine and asked for forty thousand rupees as advance to book it. As soon as I transferred the money he stopped answering my calls, blocked my number, and there was never any car. The account he gave was in a false name.
cases.notes: Deception from the outset inducing delivery of money -> BNS 318 cheating.

cases.complaint: A man came to my house saying he was an officer from my bank. He showed an identity card with the bank's logo and said my account had to be upgraded urgently or it would be frozen. Believing him, I gave him twenty-five thousand rupees in cash. Later the bank told me they have no such officer and never sent anyone.
cases.notes: Cheating by pretending to be someone else (a bank officer) -> BNS 319 cheating by personation, which builds on 318.

cases.complaint: My neighbour is angry that I filed a police complaint against his son. Yesterday he came to my gate and threatened that if I do not take back my complaint he will kill me and burn down my house with my family inside. I am genuinely afraid for the safety of my family.
cases.notes: Threat of injury to person/property to cause alarm and force an act -> BNS 351 criminal intimidation.

cases.complaint: For the last one week an unknown man keeps calling me. He says he knows where my children study and that if I do not stop giving evidence in the court case he will harm my daughter and destroy my family. He repeats these threats every day and I am living in constant fear.
cases.notes: Repeated threats of harm to deter a lawful act (giving evidence) -> BNS 351 criminal intimidation.

cases.complaint: A local rowdy comes to my shop every Friday and forces me to hand over five thousand rupees. He says that if I refuse to pay he will smash my shop, spoil my goods and beat me up so that I cannot do business. Out of fear I have been paying him every week for the last three months.
cases.notes: Delivery of money obtained by putting a person in fear of injury -> BNS 308 extortion. Note the corpus title for 308 is a definitional fragment; the offence is extortion.

cases.complaint: Because of an old enmity over a boundary, my neighbour deliberately went into my field at night and set fire to my haystack and standing wheat crop. A large part of my crop, worth about eighty thousand rupees, was completely burnt and destroyed. He did it only to cause me loss.

expected.title: Mischief by injury, inundation, fire or explosive substance, etc

cases.notes: Intentional destruction of property causing wrongful loss (by fire, to crops) -> BNS 324 mischief (aggravated sub-clauses for fire/agriculture live under 324).

cases.complaint: My business partner made a false property sale deed. He forged my signature on it to make it look as if I had agreed to sell my share of our land, and then used that fake document at the registration office to transfer the land into his own name. I never signed any such deed and never agreed to any sale.

expected.title: Forgery of valuable security, will, etc

cases.notes: Making a false document (forged signature on a sale deed = valuable security) -> BNS 336 forgery, aggravated by 338; using it as genuine (340) may also surface.

cases.complaint: My younger brother was walking on the footpath by the roadside in the morning. A speeding truck driver, driving rashly and talking on his phone, lost control, mounted the footpath and ran over my brother. My brother died on the spot. The driver had no intention to kill anyone but he was driving very carelessly.
cases.notes: Death caused by a rash/negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide -> BNS 106 causing death by negligence.

cases.complaint: As I was leaving through the main gate of our housing society, the watchman along with two other men deliberately stood in my way and physically blocked my path. They would not let me pass and kept me standing at the gate against my will for over an hour, even though I have every right to use that gate.
cases.notes: Voluntarily obstructing a person so as to prevent them from proceeding -> BNS 126 wrongful restraint (not confinement, since only one direction was blocked).

cases.complaint: The accused runs a garage. We found that he has been buying motorcycles that he knows were stolen, keeping them in his garage, changing their number plates and reselling them cheaply to others. He was fully aware that these vehicles were stolen when he took them.
cases.notes: Dishonestly receiving/retaining property known to be stolen -> BNS 317 (dishonestly receiving stolen property).

cases.complaint: I just wanted to ask about the office timings of the passport seva kendra and what documents I need to bring to apply for a fresh passport for my son. Someone told me the police station would know the procedure, so I came to ask here.
cases.notes: A civil/administrative enquiry describing no offence -> map_sections should return status=no_grounded_match (no BNS section).

cases.complaint: My daughter scored very high marks in her twelfth board examinations and has got admission into a good engineering college. I am extremely happy and proud, and I just wanted to share this good news with everyone at the station today.
cases.notes: No crime, no complaint -> map_sections should refuse with status=no_grounded_match.
